question: I want fine-tuning an OpenAI model to hand back another usable LM, not just a remote job id. Which model names select the OpenAI provider automatically, what training formats are accepted, and what provider-side IDs and cleanup state does DSPy track?
gold_answer: OpenAI fine-tuning is auto-selected only for model strings starting with `openai/` or `ft:`. The provider accepts only chat and completion training data. `OpenAIProvider.finetune` saves JSONL locally, uploads it, stores the upload id on `job.provider_file_id`, starts remote training and stores the remote job id on `job.provider_job_id`, waits for completion, and returns the provider's fine-tuned model name. `LM._run_finetune_job` then turns that string into a copied `dspy.LM`, so `job.result()` is another LM instance. `TrainingJobOpenAI.cancel()` also cancels the provider job and deletes the uploaded file if it still exists.

rubric.statement: When `LM` infers a provider automatically, it selects `OpenAIProvider()` only for model strings that start with `openai/` or `ft:`; otherwise it falls back to the base `Provider()`.
OpenAI fine-tuning accepts only `TrainDataFormat.CHAT` and `TrainDataFormat.COMPLETION`, and `OpenAIProvider.finetune` validates the requested format before continuing.

`OpenAIProvider.finetune` saves the training data with `save_data`, uploads it, stores the returned upload id on `job.provider_file_id`, starts remote fine-tuning with that file and stores the returned job id on `job.provider_job_id`, waits for completion, and then returns the provider-reported fine-tuned model name.
`LM._run_finetune_job` takes the model string returned by `provider.finetune`, creates a copied `LM` with `self.copy(model=model)`, and sets that `LM` object as the training job result.

`TrainingJobOpenAI.cancel()` cancels an existing nonterminal provider job, clears `provider_job_id`, deletes the uploaded provider file if it still exists, clears `provider_file_id`, and then calls the base `cancel()` logic.
